text:
Sam: Kickoff — Acme POC perf plan. Need to lock load pattern and confirm billing for spike tests. @Priya can you own the load plan? @Liam can you confirm Dedicated pool availability WED 09:00 PST?
Priya: Yep. Plan proposal: baseline (8k seq, 50 qps for 10m) and burst (200 qps bursts for 2m, repeated). They want 99th < 250ms. Thoughts on model/config?
Liam: Dedicated pool available Wed 09:00-11:00 PST. For latency, rdm-1 (optimized) gives best tail latency; rdm-1-quant trades a bit of latency for cost. Enable prefix/KV cache for repeated prompts to help p99.
Jenna: Heads up — Acme's security team wants E2E encryption, KMS proof, and audit log retention spelled out before we run anything. They flagged Private deployment as preferred. For POC we can provide a scoped answer and temporary logs, but questionnaire needs an owner.
Sam: We can't start the real runs until security Q is at least "acceptable". Priya, can you own the answers? I'll offer a scoped NDA addendum if needed.
Priya: I'll draft. Need owners for specific sections: @Jenna for logs/audit, @Liam for network isolation, @Sam for legal/contract. Draft in internal doc: https://redwood.internal/docs/partners/acme-security-draft.md
perf-bot: Test runner scheduled: job-id 55872 queued for 2026-03-25 09:00:00 PST. Attached baseline config.
Liam: Quick config note — set batch_size=8 for low-latency run. Command I'll run locally:```
rwood run --pool dedicated-acme --model rdm-1 --batch 8 --qps 50 --duration 600
```
Priya: Pricing question from Acme: will bursts be billed at committed reserved rate or on-demand? Sam, can sales confirm possible POC discount for burst usage?
Sam: Usage-billed. Committed reserved capacity reduces unit price. For the POC we can offer a temporary 20% usage discount if they sign an LOI within 30 days — I'll confirm with finance and send a note.
Jenna: Post-run notes (baseline): p95 ~120ms, p99 ~340ms — saw tail spikes from context fetches. Also observed an OOM on worker-3 at minute 7 (investigating). Recommend enabling KV cache and retesting.
Priya: Quick summary: baseline OK for steady 50 qps. Burst at 200 qps without cache failed p99 SLO. Root cause: cache misses and a few oversized sequences. Recommend: enable KV cache, cap max_seq to 4k for bursts, and try quantized variant to reduce memory pressure.
Liam: I'll spin rdm-1-quant with kernel opts and run an optimized test in 30m. perf-bot will post artifacts.
perf-bot: Run 55873 started. Artifacts: https://redwood.internal/artifacts/55873/summary.json
Sam: Customer follow-up — Acme asked about support SLA during ramp. For enterprise add-on we can offer 24/7 chat + 4hr response. Is that sufficient for POC?
Jenna: For the trial, yes. Also confirm we can provide 30-day audit logs; security team requested retention details. We can commit to 30 days for POC.
Priya: Landing plan: run optimized config, capture latency histograms + flame graphs, produce 1-page results and 1-slide exec summary. Aim to deliver by Friday EOD.
Sam: Thanks. @Liam please paste final perf numbers when the run completes. I'll draft the pricing note for the customer with both options (reduce burst vs capacity upgrade).
Liam: Final numbers from run 55873 (quant + KV cache): baseline 50 qps => p50 45ms, p95 110ms, p99 220ms. Burst 200 qps => p50 60ms, p95 150ms, p99 260ms. GPU mem stable, CPU/GPU util steady, no OOMs this time.
Priya: Noted — burst p99 is 260ms, slightly over their 250ms target. Options: drop burst cap to 180 qps (p99 ~240ms) or upgrade the reserved pool (+estimated cost in slide). I'll include both in the doc.
Sam: I'll propose two commercial options to Acme: (A) keep current pool, limit burst to 180 qps, 20% POC usage discount; (B) increase reserved capacity with guaranteed latency SLO (pricing delta in the draft). Sending draft to the customer after QA.
Jenna: Attached short runbook for canary and rollback steps in case latency regresses during their ramp.
Priya: I'll finalize the short results doc and a single slide for the execs and link it here when ready.
Sam: Great work everyone. We'll reconvene if Acme asks for a follow-up deep-dive.
